I did not find the Tier 1 baptism or marriage in the indexed public web results.

The strongest find is still the **1918 probate calendar card**, which does support the Killoscully identity but does **not** add Honora’s maiden name. The card reads, in substance: **“Gleeson, Patrick — Munnia, Killoscully, Newport, Co. Tipperary, Labourer — Limerick D.R. Will — Grant 11 March 1918 — Execx. Honora Gleeson, widow.”** The image also shows the adjacent Newport-area Gleeson entries you flagged: **John Gleeson of Verryleigh**, farmer, will granted 26 March 1918; and **Patrick Gleeson of Ballynanoose, Glenculloo, Newport**, farmer, administration granted 23 Dec. 1918 to **Cath. Gleeson**. I see no relationship language between the three entries, and no maiden name for Honora on the calendar card itself. 

For the baptism target, the right parish is searchable in principle but I did not get a public indexed hit for **Michael Gleeson, son of Patrick Gleeson + Honora O’Brien**, in the web-visible indexes. NLI confirms **Ballinahinch and Killoscully** has baptisms **7 Jul 1839–7 Feb 1874** and marriages **26 Jan 1853–4 Feb 1874**, exactly covering the hypothesized window. ([registers.nli.ie][1]) RootsIreland’s North Tipperary coverage says **Ballinahinch/Killoscully** has RC baptisms **1839–1899** and marriages **1853–1899**, and **Newport-Birdhill** has baptisms and marriages from **1795–1911**, so the Tier 1 search should be technically available there even if not freely exposed in Google/Bing snippets. ([rootsireland.ie][2])

I also checked for the exact combinations **“Michael Gleeson” + “Honora O’Brien”**, **“Patrick Gleeson” + “Honora O’Brien” + Killoscully**, and **“Michael Gleeson” + “Patrick Gleeson” + “Honora” + Newport/Tipperary**. No match surfaced for the desired baptism or marriage. That is not a kill; it mostly means the desired record is not indexed visibly on the open web, or is indexed behind RootsIreland/Findmypast/Ancestry without snippet exposure.

There is useful cluster context from Griffith’s Valuation: Killoscully has a dense Gleeson cluster, including Patrick/Patk entries at **Lackagh**, **Shallee (Coughlan)**, **Curraheen**, and **Shallee (White)**, plus Michael, John, James, Martin, Daniel, Denis, etc. It also has O’Brien entries at **Knockmeale** and **Shallee (Coughlan)**. This supports Killoscully as a plausible Gleeson/O’Brien neighborhood, but it does not tie your Patrick + Honora to Michael. ([failteromhat.com][3])

On the Naas side, I found a 1901 Naas census index entry for **John Hayde**, age 69, born Co. Tipperary, retired R.I.C. sergeant, at **20 Dublin Road West, Naas**, with wife Elizabeth and children Patrick, Elizabeth, and Esther A. That looks relevant to Johanna Hayde’s father-side household, but Johanna herself is not shown in that household in the indexed extract. ([creeore.com][4]) I also found a **Michael Gleeson**, age 20, born Co. Tipperary, shop assistant, boarding at **10.1 Main Street West, Naas** in 1901, but he is much too young to be the 1888 groom unless the marriage record age/context has been misunderstood; I would treat him as a separate Naas Tipperary-Gleeson cluster lead, not the target groom. ([creeore.com][4])

Checked-negative summary: no public indexed hit found for Michael’s Killoscully/Newport baptism; no public indexed hit found for a Patrick Gleeson + Honora O’Brien marriage; no probate-calendar image evidence found naming Honora’s maiden name; no indexed record found linking the 1918 Munnia Patrick to the Verryleigh/Ballynanoose Newport Gleesons.

Current status: **not upgraded to T2 yet**, but also **not killed**. The next highest-yield action is a paid/indexed search in RootsIreland North Tipperary for: child **Michael Gleeson**, father **Patrick**, mother **Honora/Norah O’Brien/Brien/Bryan/Brine**, parish **Ballinahinch/Killoscully** and then **Newport-Birdhill**, 1853–1874. The second-best action is the same query for siblings, not just Michael, because one sibling baptism with “O’Brien” at Munnia/Killoscully would materially strengthen the linkage.
